lines.caption: This is a tour of the pull request for issue 149: Ctrl+F now searches subfolders too.
lines.say: This is a tour of the pull request for issue one forty-nine: Control F now searches subfolders too.

lines.caption: It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Two default shortcuts swap, and the Go menu gains Search in Subfolders. Nothing else about searching changes.
Ctrl+F used to search only this folder. Now it searches the folder and its subfolders.
lines.say: Control F used to search only this folder. Now it searches the folder and its subfolders.

lines.caption: Ctrl+F is now the key of the subfolder action, labelled Search in Subfolders in menus.
lines.say: Control F is now the key of the subfolder action, labelled Search in Subfolders in menus.

lines.caption: That action saves the scope as on, so the toggle shows pressed and subfolder matches are listed.
Ctrl+Shift+F used to include subfolders. Now it searches only the folder you're in.
lines.say: Control Shift F used to include subfolders. Now it searches only the folder you're in.

lines.caption: It is now the key of the folder action, labelled Search for Files.
That action saves the scope as off, so the toggle shows released and only this folder's files are listed.
The Go menu now lists Search in Subfolders first, above Search for Files.
Shortcuts you changed yourself stay, because they're stored by action name, and the names are unchanged.
The toolbar Search button and the Search key still open with the folder's saved choice.
Issue 139 gave each scope its own shortcut. You search subfolders more often, so that one gets the easier key.
lines.say: Issue one thirty-nine gave each scope its own shortcut. You search subfolders more often, so that one gets the easier key.

lines.caption: Only the default keys move. Each action keeps its name, label, tooltip and behaviour.
Adding Search in Subfolders to the Go menu was the issue's optional suggestion, and it's done.
This table lists every way to open a search, and what it searches before and after this PR.
The whole code change: two keys swapped in the action table, and one line added to the Go menu.
Each menu label stays with its behaviour, so the menu items just show the other shortcut.
Select by Pattern still mentions Ctrl+F. Both searches match words the same way, so it stays true.
lines.say: Select by Pattern still mentions Control F. Both searches match words the same way, so it stays true.

lines.caption: The explainer for issue 139 is kept as the record of that PR.
lines.say: The explainer for issue one thirty-nine is kept as the record of that pull request.

lines.caption: The PR changes one source file, moves one verify script, updates another, and adds this page.
To undo it, revert the PR. Saved scopes and your own shortcuts are untouched either way.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was built and tested in the cloud container on the first commit. The Go menu line came later, so CI tests it first.
lines.say: It was built and tested in the cloud container on the first commit. The Go menu line came later, so C I tests it first.

lines.caption: It swaps the keys of the actions from issue 139, and checks every script the issue listed.
lines.say: It swaps the keys of the actions from issue one thirty-nine, and checks every script the issue listed.

lines.caption: The first commit built with no warnings in the changed files, and its packages were installed.
The moved verify script passed: Ctrl+F found both files, and Ctrl+Shift+F found only the top one.
lines.say: The moved verify script passed: Control F found both files, and Control Shift F found only the top one.

lines.caption: The toggle spacing test, four unchanged search tests, the toggle test and the smoke test all passed too.
The Go menu line and a renamed check came after that run, so they weren't run here. CI runs them.
lines.say: The Go menu line and a renamed check came after that run, so they weren't run here. C I runs them.

lines.caption: Not run yet: the full set of 34 verify scripts, and the audit of CI's screenshots.
lines.say: Not run yet: the full set of thirty-four verify scripts, and the audit of C I's screenshots.

lines.caption: The local review at high level found three things before the first push, and all three were fixed.
It renamed a check in the new verify script that still carried the old mapping's name.
It also found the explainer missing, and the Ctrl+F item in no menu. This page and the Go menu line fix those.
lines.say: It also found the explainer missing, and the Control F item in no menu. This page and the Go menu line fix those.

lines.caption: CI reviews every code push as well, in its code review comment on this PR.
lines.say: C I reviews every code push as well, in its code review comment on this pull request.

lines.caption: After the merge, every verify script runs on main, and your own Thunar gets the new keys at its next install.
The changes, CI's results and both issues are linked here.
Part 3. What comes later.
No open issue depends on this one. It is the last group of its batch, after issues 144 and 150.
lines.say: No open issue depends on this one. It is the last group of its batch, after issues one forty-four and one fifty.

lines.caption: So this PR stands alone for now, with nothing planned after it.
lines.say: So this pull request stands alone for now, with nothing planned after it.

lines.caption: In short: Ctrl+F now includes subfolders, Ctrl+Shift+F searches only the folder, and your own shortcuts stay.
lines.say: In short: Control F now includes subfolders, Control Shift F searches only the folder, and your own shortcuts stay.
